result.title: GateTrace: Where Do Crowd Crossings Go Missing Under Occlusion?
result.summary: At large events, pedestrian tracking supports entrance and passageway counts, but totals hide which crossings were missed. In a stadium study, the system recorded about four in five clearly visible crossings but fewer than one in three mostly obscured crossings. The videos lacked trajectories annotated across frames, so we turned to MOT20, which provides pedestrian trajectories and visibility. We introduce GateTrace to locate missed crossings and assess changes to counting rules. It derives reference crossings from annotations under fixed rules, matches reports by person, direction, time and position, and traces misses through saved boxes and counting decisions. With a shared detector, ByteTrack, OC-SORT and BoT-SORT recover 38.9-46.7% of low-visibility reference crossings on development sequences, versus 98.1-99.0% at high visibility. The gap recurs on two further sequences under a protocol fixed in advance. Published outputs of MOT20-tuned BASE recover 63-78% at low visibility across both sequence groups. Losses stop at different stages across systems. Across four systems and both groups, 47-79% of low-visibility misses have no nearby output linked to the person or no possible crossing in the saved tracks. Removing later checks from BASE on development sequences leaves most misses unresolved and lowers precision against the fixed reference list from about 96% to 77%. Misses also remain among sampled reference crossings that two human annotators supported after checking the videos. GateTrace shows where crossings are lost and measures the recovery and precision costs of changing later checks. We will release the code and per-crossing records.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究人群计数中遮挡导致的漏计：以 MOT20 的轨迹与可见度标注为参照，提出 GateTrace 按人物、方向、时间和位置匹配计数记录，定位漏失发生在跟踪输出还是后续计数规则环节，并量化规则改动的召回与精度代价。
AI.relevance_reason: 其按流水线阶段追溯「视觉证据在哪一步丢失」的评测思路，可能可供核查 LVR 中遮挡或低可见度下任务必要视觉细节在感知、关联到决策各环节的信息坍缩与证据筛选问题。
